question: Does adaptive block-size (EMA of acceptance) beat fixed block=5 on DFlash 31B?
verdict: NOT WORTH IT — fixed block=5 is near-optimal; adaptive headroom <~4% and only on creative prose.

code.note: steep penalty below 5 — cannot safely shrink

why_marginal: code needs bs>=5 (bs3 = 21 vs bs5 = 31), prose barely prefers bs3 over bs5 (+3.7%, flat & noisy). A single accept->block policy (bs=round(accept+pad)) cannot satisfy both optima; best overall gain ~1-2%, below measurement noise.
real_ceiling: The prose weak spot (1.6x, accept 2.16) is DRAFT-ACCEPTANCE-bound, not block-bound. Only a better/larger draft (or tree drafting) lifts it — block tuning cannot.
adaptive_ab_status: A/B run aborted by GPU Timeout under heavy contention from the concurrent custom-engine benchmarking; not retried — verdict already established by the static probe, and further MLX GPU load corrupts the concurrent session's measurements.
recommendation: Keep fixed block=5. Stop MLX-side GPU experiments; the remaining speed lever (native block-verify engine) is owned by the concurrent session and needs a clean GPU to measure.
